Question: Let \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) be three positive real numbers whose sum is \(1.\) If no one of these numbers is more than twice any other, then the minimum possible value of the product \(xyz\) is
Solution:
The conditions are unchanged by reordering, so assume \(x\le y\le z\). The ratio restriction then says \(z\le2x\). With \(y\) fixed, making the smallest entry smaller and the largest entry larger decreases their product. We can make this move until their ratio reaches \(2\).

Set
\[
\delta=\frac{2x-z}{3}\ge0,
\qquad u=x-\delta=\frac{x+z}{3}>0.
\]
Then \(z+\delta=2u\), and
\[
u\le x\le y\le z\le2u.
\]
Thus the new triple \((u,y,2u)\) still satisfies the ratio restriction and has sum \(1\). Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
u(2u)
&=(x-\delta)(z+\delta)\\
&=xz-\delta(z-x)-\delta^2\le xz.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplying by \(y>0\) gives \(xyz\ge2u^2y\).

Write \(t=y/u\). The ordering gives \(1\le t\le2\), and the sum condition gives \(u(t+3)=1\). Therefore
\[
2u^2y=\frac{2t}{(t+3)^3}.
\]
To compare this with \(1/32\), factor the difference after multiplying by the positive denominator:
\[
64t-(t+3)^3
=(t-1)(27-10t-t^2).
\]
For \(1\le t\le2\), the first factor is nonnegative and the second is at least \(27-20-4=3\). Consequently,
\[
xyz\ge\frac{2t}{(t+3)^3}\ge\frac1{32}.
\]
Equality requires \(\delta=0\) and \(t=1\), giving \((x,y,z)=(1/4,1/4,1/2)\) in this ordering. This triple satisfies every condition. Hence the minimum is \(\boxed{1/32}\), choice A, attained at its permutations.
